summary: A mid-heavy euro where you build a troupe of artist cards whose power depends on turn order, then tour a point-to-point map hiring artists and staging performances that trigger area-majority scoring in towns and cities. Turns are tight optimization puzzles about sequencing hires and performances before rivals lock up the best town slots or artist combos.
praised: Clever artist card system where positional/order effects create real hand-management puzzles
Smooth production and iconography for a fairly dense ruleset
Satisfying engine-building feel as your troupe compounds in efficiency
Good table presence and theme integration for a euro
criticised: Fair amount of rules overhead and a slow-to-click first play
Can feel like parallel optimization with only intermittent direct clashes over map/majority spots
Some downtime in higher player counts
End-game scoring can feel a bit swingy relative to the mid-game decisions

interaction.kind: area majority contests over limited town/city performance slots, otherwise mostly parallel engine-building

scoring.why: fame comes from performance payouts, area-majority bonuses in towns/cities, artist-card synergies, and end-game bonus cards, so the winner is usually whoever balanced several of these rather than maxing one

similar: Merv: The Heart of the Silk Road
